intent: A sunken amphitheatre of the gods: a long gold-lit stair cut down through terraces of gilded seats into a broad arena, with a great gold fire bowl holding a pillar of holy fire at its heart, so the approach itself is the ceremony.
variation: way in: one stair (the road down and back round the fire) / two opposite stairs (the road crosses the arena) / two crossed stairs (it bends round the fire)
bowl: round / an oval stretched along the main stair / a squared great court
seats: three tiers / four / five / three with a fallen sector walked down through the seats as rubble
rim: open / a colonnade ring of ivory columns / ruined fragments and fallen drums on the paving
heart: the great fire bowl alone / ringed by six standing waystones / ringed by four braziers
the stair's side (north, south, east or west), its lateral offset, the footprint (44 to 56 cells a side) and the arc the road takes round the fire

critic.reads_as_itself: yes: an amphitheatre stepping down to a central bowl under a pillar of light
critic.best_shot: feature-shots-final, column 2: down the gold-checkered stair into the arena with the bowl
critic.why: Clean, symmetrical, unmistakably built; held back by one bowl layout across seeds and a fire bowl that reads as a table.

role: A side court and event arena: the amphitheatre for a boss or a gathering, reached down its processional stair.
notes:
# B: Amphitheatre of the gods

Keep: the concentric gold-and-ivory tiers stepping down to a round arena are clean, symmetrical and unmistakably built. The checkered paving and the stair cut through the seats are right for the Domain.

1. The fire bowl reads as a round café table on three splayed legs. Give it a solid stepped pedestal or a ring of short columns under the bowl, and set it on a raised dais, so it reads as an altar that holds a pillar of fire.
2. The seeds are one bowl in different sizes and ovalness. Vary the plan: half-bowls open on one side to a drop, two arenas joined by the stair, the stair coming in from a corner, so the road meets it differently each time.
3. The grey stone gate frame on the rim is weathered, menhir-grey and leans. Make it ivory and gold, square and plumb, and use it as a proper entrance at the top of the processional stair.
